answers.question: Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?
answers.answer: - No, a 16‑mile run would break the taper and add unnecessary fatigue. A short, easy run keeps your legs loose without compromising race readiness.

new.analysis: The athlete’s latest week (Oct 5–11) was a light taper week with 34 mi and no hard effort. The goal is a 3:45 marathon on Oct 18, and we are in the final taper phase. The plan for Oct 12–18 must keep volume low, keep heart rate in easy zones, and avoid any new hard or long work. The athlete asked if a 16‑mi run on Wednesday would help; the answer is no – a longer run would upset the taper and add fatigue. The main job is to keep legs fresh, stay below 150 bpm, do a brief quality stimulus (a single mile at marathon pace), and provide a short easy run on Saturday to set the rhythm. I will flag volume, rest, HR drift, race‑prep, and recovery. No medical issues, so no safety callouts. The next week’s plan is straightforward with mostly rest and short easy runs.
